videoReviews.credit: NOAA Ocean Exploration, 2023 Shakedown + EXPRESS West Coast Exploration
videoReviews.inspectionMethod: Six individually opened source frames sampled at roughly 5,15,25,35,45,55 seconds. No claim of continuous playback or audio review.
observedSequence: Wide rocky steps with an octopus left of a pink coral colony and several pale attached animals. Opening slate identifies Quinault Canyon off Washington, 1612m.
Closer octopus spreads several arms over rock ledges.
Octopus remains spread across steps; arm tips curl upward.
Closer view as mantle and arms shift toward lower-right rock gap.
Mantle lower near edge; arms curled and extended around the rock.
Octopus lower/right partly behind rock lip while credits appear.
videoReviews.primaryCaption: Muusoctopus at 1650m with moving brittle stars on surrounding seafloor.
videoReviews.reason: Published clip differs materially from the page's sandy-seafloor scene and depth. Do not adopt caption as exact identification proof until source mapping is resolved. No YouTube watch identity was found on the page or bounded searches.
videoReviews.rights: NOAA credit and FAQ support public-domain footage absent an exception; no exception visible. Rights do not resolve source-caption identity mismatch.
videoReviews.thumbnailDecision: No new thumbnail admitted. Existing 640x360 poster from prior source34 has not been relabeled to match this different rocky sequence.

retiredDrafts.title: I was still holding on
retiredDrafts.body:
One arm went down the crack. I kept the others on top while it investigated.

Then I followed it.

There was still something holding me back. It took a while to persuade that arm that the rest of us had made a decision.
retiredDrafts.reason: Concrete draft based on rock-gap sequence, but its hesitation and distributed-grip device are too close to Elspeth's existing holding-ground episode and newly admitted Mina movement problem. Source mismatch independently blocks admission.
